title: Kinematics
summary: Wheel speeds to robot speeds, the WPILib way.

steps.title: Wheel speeds in, robot speeds out

say.never: Last lesson you worked out the robot's speed with your own math. WPILib, the robot toolkit, has a class that does it for you: `DifferentialDriveKinematics`. You give it the two wheel speeds, and it gives back the robot's forward speed and turning speed together in a single object called `ChassisSpeeds`.
say.bit: `DifferentialDriveKinematics` does the math you wrote by hand last lesson.

say.never: Hold down **Ctrl** and tap **P**. A small search box pops up at the top. Type `DifferentialDriveMech`, then press **Enter**. It finds any file by its name, so you never have to dig through folders.
say.bit: Press **Ctrl+P**, type `DifferentialDriveMech` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name, so you never have to dig through folders.

say.never: Click in the code, then hold **Ctrl** and tap **F**. Search for `getChassisSpeeds`, then fill it in with the board's code.
say.bit: Press **Ctrl+F** and search for `getChassisSpeeds`, then fill it in.

say.never: Your code only works once it's started. Press **Start** and wait until the status says **Running**.
